body.en: In *textual* (descriptive) presentation, data are given in a paragraph. It is good for a small amount of data and lets us stress certain points, but with many figures the reader must go through the whole text to understand it.
body.kn: ಪಠ್ಯ ನಿರೂಪಣೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ದತ್ತಾಂಶವನ್ನು ಪ್ಯಾರಾಗ್ರಾಫ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ನೀಡುತ್ತೇವೆ. ಕಡಿಮೆ ದತ್ತಾಂಶಕ್ಕೆ ಸೂಕ್ತ, ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಅಂಕಿಗಳಿದ್ದರೆ ಕಷ್ಟ.

title.en: On the board: Parts of a table

say.en: Every table has a number and a title that says what, where and when.
Column headings are captions. Row headings are stubs.
The body holds the figures. Failed is total minus passed: 50 minus 30 is 20.
Below the table come the source note and footnotes, so readers can check the data.

body.en: A *table* arranges data in rows and columns. Its parts are: table number, title, captions (column headings), stubs (row headings), body (the figures), unit of measurement, source note and footnotes. Tables may be classified by time, place, quality or quantity.
body.kn: ಕೋಷ್ಟಕದ ಭಾಗಗಳು: ಕೋಷ್ಟಕ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ, ಶೀರ್ಷಿಕೆ, ಕಾಲಂ ಶೀರ್ಷಿಕೆ (ಕ್ಯಾಪ್ಶನ್), ಸಾಲು ಶೀರ್ಷಿಕೆ (ಸ್ಟಬ್), ಮುಖ್ಯ ಭಾಗ, ಅಳತೆಯ ಘಟಕ, ಮೂಲ ಟಿಪ್ಪಣಿ.

Why is a table easier to read than the sentence in the example?
Keep passed below the total, or failed turns negative!

problem.en: Tabulate: "Out of 120 students, 50 were boys of whom 30 passed, and of the 70 girls 56 passed."

steps.en: Stubs (rows): Boys, Girls, Total. Captions (columns): Passed, Failed, Total.
Boys: passed 30, failed 50 − 30 = 20, total 50. Girls: passed 56, failed 70 − 56 = 14, total 70.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Tabulate: "Out of 120 students, 50 were boys of whom 30 passed, and of the 70 girls 56 passed."

say.en: Let us work this out together. Tabulate: "Out of 120 students, 50 were boys of whom 30 passed, and of the 70 girls 56 passed.".
Stubs rows: Boys, Girls, Total. Captions columns: Passed, Failed, Total.
Boys: passed 30, failed 50 minus 30 equals 20, total 50. Girls: passed 56, failed 70 minus 56 equals 14, total 70.
Total: passed 86, failed 34, total 120. Check: 86 plus 34 equals 120.
So the answer is Boys 30 over 20/50, Girls 56 over 14/70, Total 86 over 34/120.
